name: Tulu
region: Coastal Karnataka (Dakshina Kannada, Udupi) and Kasaragod, Kerala
description: Dravidian language with a rich oral tradition of paddanas, ballads sung during field work and in bhuta kola rituals.

name: Kodava
description: Language of the Kodava people of the Kodagu hills; traditionally oral, now usually written in Kannada script.

name: Beary
description: Spoken by the Beary community of the Karnataka coast; draws on Malayalam and Tulu.

name: Havyaka Kannada
region: Uttara Kannada, Shivamogga and Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka
description: Kannada dialect of the Havyaka community that keeps many older Kannada forms.

name: Badaga
description: Closely related to Kannada; spoken by the Badaga community of the Nilgiri hills.

name: Toda
description: Dravidian language of the pastoral Toda people, known for its unusual sounds and its sung poetry.

name: Kota
description: Spoken by the Kota community of artisans and musicians in a few Nilgiri villages.

name: Irula
region: Nilgiris and Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu; Attappadi, Kerala
description: Dravidian language of the Irula people, related to Tamil.

name: Saurashtra
region: Madurai and other towns of Tamil Nadu
description: Indo-Aryan language of silk-weaving communities whose ancestors came from Gujarat; it has its own script.

name: Paniya
region: Wayanad, Kerala, and neighbouring Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
description: Dravidian language of the Paniya people of the Wayanad plateau.

name: Jeseri
description: Island variety close to Malayalam, spoken across the Lakshadweep islands.

name: Yerukula
description: Dravidian language of the Yerukala community, related to Tamil.

name: Koya
region: Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha
description: Dravidian language of the Koya people, closely related to Gondi.

name: Lambadi
region: Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra
description: Indo-Aryan language of the Banjara community, written in the script of whichever state its speakers live in.

name: Gondi
region: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Telangana
description: Dravidian language of the Gond people, one of India's largest Adivasi communities, with many regional varieties.

name: Kurukh
region: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and West Bengal
description: Dravidian language of the Oraon people.

name: Kui
description: Dravidian language of the Kondh people.

name: Kuvi
region: Southern Odisha and northern Andhra Pradesh
description: Kondh language closely related to Kui.

name: Sora
region: Southern Odisha and northern Andhra Pradesh
description: Munda language with its own script, Sorang Sompeng.

name: Juang
description: Munda language of the Juang people of the Odisha hills.

name: Bonda
description: Munda language of the Bonda (Remo) people, spoken in a small group of hill villages.

name: Santali
region: Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Assam
description: The largest Munda language, written in its own Ol Chiki script.

name: Ho
description: Munda language with its own Warang Citi script.

name: Mundari
description: Munda language of the Munda people.

name: Halbi
region: Bastar, Chhattisgarh, and neighbouring Odisha and Maharashtra
description: Indo-Aryan language long used as a common tongue across the communities of Bastar.

name: Chhattisgarhi
description: Eastern Hindi language with a strong folk tradition, including Pandavani storytelling.

name: Bhili
region: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
description: Indo-Aryan language of the Bhil people, with many regional varieties.

name: Nihali
region: A few villages of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
description: A language isolate: unrelated to any of its neighbours.

name: Warli
region: Palghar and Thane, Maharashtra, and southern Gujarat
description: Language of the Warli people, also known for Warli painting.

name: Katkari
description: Indo-Aryan language of the Katkari community.

name: Konkani (Goan)
region: Goa and the Konkan coast of Karnataka and Maharashtra
description: Indo-Aryan language written in different scripts by different communities.

name: Malvani
description: Konkani variety of the southern Konkan coast, home of the Dashavatar folk theatre.

name: Kutchi
description: Sindhi-related language of Kutch, usually written in Gujarati script.

name: Marwari
description: Rajasthani language of the Marwar region, with a long tradition of ballads and folk songs.

name: Bundeli
region: Bundelkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
description: Western Hindi language, known for the sung Alha ballads.

name: Awadhi
description: Eastern Hindi language of Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas.

name: Bhojpuri
region: Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh; diaspora in Mauritius, Fiji and Suriname
description: Widely spoken, with a large tradition of folk songs, but little written material.

name: Maithili
region: Mithila region of Bihar and Nepal
description: Language of Mithila, historically written in its own Tirhuta script.

name: Magahi
description: Bihari language of the old Magadha region.

name: Garhwali
description: Central Pahari language of the Garhwal Himalaya.

name: Kumaoni
description: Central Pahari language of the Kumaon hills.

name: Jaunsari
description: Western Pahari language of the Jaunsar-Bawar region.

name: Kangri
description: Western Pahari language of the Kangra valley.

name: Kinnauri
description: Tibeto-Burman language of the Kinnaur valley.

name: Dogri
description: Language of the Jammu region.

name: Ladakhi
description: Tibetic language of Ladakh, written in Tibetan script.

name: Lepcha
region: Sikkim and the Darjeeling hills, West Bengal
description: Language of the Lepcha (Róng) people, with its own script.

name: Limbu
description: Kiranti language with its own script.

name: Sikkimese
description: Tibetic language of the Bhutia people of Sikkim.

name: Toto
description: Spoken only in the village of Totopara; a Toto script was created recently.

name: Bodo
description: Tibeto-Burman language of the Bodo people.

name: Mising
description: Tani language of the Mising people of the Brahmaputra valley.

name: Karbi
description: Tibeto-Burman language of the Karbi people.

name: Dimasa
description: Tibeto-Burman language of the Dimasa people.

name: Rabha
description: Tibeto-Burman language of the Rabha people.

name: Kokborok
description: Tibeto-Burman language of Tripura's indigenous communities.

name: Khasi
description: Austroasiatic language of the Khasi people.

name: Garo
description: Tibeto-Burman language of the Garo people.

name: Mizo
description: Kuki-Chin language of Mizoram.

name: Meitei
description: Language of Manipur, with its own Meitei Mayek script.

name: Tangkhul
description: Naga language of the Tangkhul people, with many village varieties.

name: Ao
description: Naga language of the Ao people.

name: Angami
description: Naga language of the Angami people.

name: Lotha
description: Naga language of the Lotha people.

name: Adi
description: Tani language of the Adi people.

name: Nyishi
description: Tani language of the Nyishi people.

name: Apatani
description: Tani language of the Apatani people of the Ziro valley.

name: Wancho
description: Naga language with its own recently created Wancho script.

name: Idu Mishmi
description: Language of the Idu Mishmi people.

name: Koro
description: Identified by linguists only in 2008; spoken in a few villages.

name: Sherdukpen
description: Language of the Sherdukpen people.

name: Great Andamanese
description: Mixed variety of the Great Andamanese languages; only a few speakers remain.

name: Onge
description: Language of the Onge people, one of the Andamans' indigenous communities.

name: Jarawa
description: Language of the Jarawa people of the Andaman forests.

name: Braj Bhasha
region: Mathura, Agra and the Braj region, Uttar Pradesh
description: Language of medieval Krishna devotional poetry such as Surdas's; still spoken around Mathura and Vrindavan.

name: Kannauji
region: Kannauj, Farrukhabad and Etawah, Uttar Pradesh
description: Western Hindi variety of the Kannauj region, close to Braj.

name: Angika
region: Bhagalpur and Munger, Bihar, and parts of Jharkhand
description: Spoken in the old Anga region of eastern Bihar, with a rich tradition of folk songs.

name: Bajjika
description: Spoken in north-western Bihar, between Maithili and Bhojpuri.

name: Surjapuri
region: Kishanganj and Purnia, Bihar, and north Bengal
description: Spoken where Bihar meets Bengal; shares features with both.

name: Gaddi
description: Language of the pastoral Gaddi shepherds who migrate across the Dhauladhar range.

name: Mandeali
description: Western Pahari variety of the Mandi valley.

name: Kullui
description: Western Pahari variety of the Kullu valley, known for its natti songs.

name: Mahasu Pahari
description: Western Pahari variety of the hills around Shimla.

name: Bhadarwahi
description: Western Pahari variety of the Bhaderwah valley.

name: Gojri
region: Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh
description: Language of the Gujjar and Bakarwal herding communities.

name: Balti
description: Tibetic language of the Balti people, spoken around Kargil.

name: Purgi
description: Tibetic language of the Purig valley around Kargil.

name: Shina
region: Dras and Gurez, Ladakh and Jammu and Kashmir
description: Dardic language spoken in a few high valleys of the western Himalaya.

name: Brokskat
description: Spoken by the Brokpa of a handful of villages on the Indus; very few speakers.

name: Bagheli
region: Rewa, Satna and Sidhi, Madhya Pradesh
description: Eastern Hindi variety of the Baghelkhand region.

name: Malvi
description: Rajasthani variety of the Malwa plateau around Indore and Ujjain.

name: Nimadi
description: Spoken in the Nimar region along the Narmada.

name: Nagpuri
description: Also called Sadri; the common language between many communities of the Chota Nagpur plateau.

name: Khortha
description: Spoken across the northern districts of Jharkhand.

name: Kurmali
description: Language of the Kurmi Mahato community, known for its jhumar songs.

name: Sambalpuri
description: Spoken across western Odisha, with a strong tradition of folk music and dance.

name: Desiya
description: Common language of the Koraput hills, used between many tribal communities.

name: Bhatri
description: Spoken by the Bhattra community of Bastar.

name: Malto
description: Dravidian language of the Sauria Paharia of the Rajmahal hills.

name: Kharia
description: Munda language of the Kharia people.

name: Birhor
description: Munda language of the small, traditionally forest-dwelling Birhor community.

name: Asur
description: Munda language of the Asur, traditional iron smelters; very few speakers.

name: Gutob
description: Munda language also known as Gadaba.

name: Parji
description: Dravidian language also known as Duruwa.

name: Kolami
description: Dravidian language of the Kolam people.

name: Mewari
description: Rajasthani variety of the Mewar region, the language of Meera's songs.

name: Dhundhari
description: Rajasthani variety of the Dhundhar region around Jaipur.

name: Shekhawati
description: Rajasthani variety of the Shekhawati region.

name: Wagdi
description: Bhili variety of southern Rajasthan.

name: Ahirani
description: Spoken across Khandesh, between Marathi, Gujarati and Bhili.

name: Varhadi
description: Marathi variety of the Varhad (Vidarbha) region.

name: Kokna
description: Language of the Kokna community of the northern Sahyadri.

name: Soliga
description: Dravidian language of the Soliga, forest dwellers of the BR hills.

name: Jenu Kurumba
region: Mysuru and Kodagu, Karnataka, and Wayanad, Kerala
description: Language of the honey-gathering Jenu Kurumba.

name: Arebhashe
description: Kannada variety of the Gowda community of Sullia and Madikeri.

name: Kundagannada
description: Kannada variety of the Kundapura region.

name: Muthuvan
description: Language of the Muthuvan community of the Idukki hills.

name: Kanikkaran
region: Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, and Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu
description: Language of the Kani people of the southern Western Ghats.

name: Konda Dora
description: Dravidian language of the Konda Dora of the Eastern Ghats.

name: Sylheti
description: Eastern Bengali-Assamese language with its own historical script, Sylheti Nagri.

name: Hajong
description: Spoken by the Hajong of the Garo Hills and the Assam plains.

name: Rajbanshi
description: Also called Kamtapuri; spoken across north Bengal and western Assam.

name: Chakma
description: Language of the Chakma people, with its own script, Ojhapath.

name: Tiwa
description: Tibeto-Burman language of the Tiwa (Lalung) people.

name: Deori
description: Tibeto-Burman language of the Deori, traditionally priests of the Chutia kingdom.

name: Galo
description: Tani language of the Galo people.

name: Tagin
description: Tani language of the Tagin people.

name: Tawang Monpa
description: Spoken by the Monpa of the Tawang valley.

name: Konyak
description: Language of the Konyak Naga, known for their tattoo and log-drum traditions.

name: Sumi
description: Language of the Sümi Naga.

name: Rengma
description: Language of the Rengma Naga.

name: Thadou
description: Kuki-Chin language of the Thadou people.

name: Hmar
description: Kuki-Chin language of the Hmar people.

name: Paite
description: Kuki-Chin language of the Paite people.

name: Zeme
region: Dima Hasao, Assam, and Peren, Nagaland
description: Language of the Zeme Naga.

name: Rongmei
description: Language of the Rongmei Naga.

name: Car Nicobarese
description: Austroasiatic language of Car Nicobar island.

name: Central Nicobarese
description: Austroasiatic language of the central Nicobar islands.

name: Shompen
description: Language of the Shompen, a small hunter-gatherer people of Great Nicobar.
